notes:
Venture 0.18 — what the controller itself is doing

• The controller's Wi-Fi strength, battery level and the time now sit in the
  top-right corner of every screen. The panel runs with the system bars off, so
  until now there was nowhere to read either of the first two, and a unit could
  go flat mid-survey without a word.
• That clock is the app's own time zone, set in Config > Controller > Time
  (the contiguous US, Arizona listed separately). A Herelink often boots with
  its clock unset — bench units have been found on GMT in Texas — and a mission
  uploaded under a time label is named from it, so a wrong zone names flights
  hours from when they flew.
• Coverage figures are corrected. The planner reported POOR camera overlap as
  GOOD, and the Lane Spacing step now shows side overlap only — the number that
  step actually changes. Worth re-checking the figures on any plan made before
  this; the flight path itself is unchanged.
• The attitude readout now warns on how far the aircraft is leaning, not only
  how fast it is moving: amber at 40 degrees, red at 45. A machine held steadily
  at 44 degrees used to read as perfectly calm.
• REVIEW joins the aircraft's network by itself and puts the controller back on
  its own network when you leave. If a saved password has stopped working it
  says so instead of waiting.
• Fly loses its Storage tab — browsing what a flight produced is REVIEW's job —
  and picks up the same chrome as the rest of the app.
• Colour means one thing now: orange is what you are touching, green is a fact
  about state. The flight bar keeps its own command colours, because there the
  colour names the command.
• Config is a page of cards, and CONFIG on the home screen sits where BACK sits
  on every other page.
• The build is minified, so this update downloads smaller and installs in about
  a third of the time.

Service: holding any home-screen card for five seconds opens the maintenance
menu, which now works — the kiosk had been blocking every entry on it silently.
USB debugging can be turned on from there, and QGroundControl opened.

Migration: none for missions or flights. The QGroundControl entry needs a unit
built on the current system image (system_venture_qgc.img); on an older image it
opens and crashes.
